Romain

real    0m13.363s
user    0m12.369s
sys     0m0.445s


So the problem is indeed in the RJavaClassLoader. What happens is that 
jython calls repeatedly findClass and expects the ClassNotFoundException.

With the double loading of RJavaClassLoader, it means that the 
URLClassLoader method fails, and the backup method fails as well, taking 
quite some time.

As said yesterday, I've put the log.txt file here ;
http://addictedtor.free.fr/misc/gabor/log.txt

which is the result of this script:

require( rJava )
.jinit( )
.jaddClassPath("jython.jar" )
rjcl <- rJava:::.rJava.class.loader
rjcl$verbose <- TRUE
jy <- .jnew( "org.python.util.PythonInterpreter" )
jy$exec( "from sympy import *" )


$ Rscript loadsympy.R > log.txt

So my question was : do we still need the alternative class lookup ? 
 From my reading of it, it looks like it only does what URLClassLoader 
does, but might be using less optimization tricks ...

Romain

messages.body_plain:
On Nov 19, 2009, at 12:06 , Edzer Pebesma wrote:

> Thanks for the answer, Simon. I still have to figure out if your  
> suggestion with the signal will work, as in our setup the Rserve  
> process runs as user rserve, and the java servlet runs in tomcat, I  
> believe under a user different from root.
>

That is entirely irrelevant since you'll be sending the signal from R  
to R so it's always the same user.


> One other question I have: do you have, or know of, a startup-script  
> (as in /etc/init.d on debian) that starts the Rserve daemon under a  
> separate user, say rserve? That would be nice to have, e.g. as part  
> of the rserve distribution. We faced some downtime after a power  
> failure; Rserve still needs manual start.
>

That is trivial - you don't need to do anything in the start script -  
just start Rserve and set gid and uid options in the config file (in  
that order!) - Rserve does the user switching automatically.

Cheers,
Simon
